comments.author: @gamelover2222
comments.text:
The lady talking about insurance probably didn't have corporate insurance.  If you are an independent contractor or self-employed, the insurance costs and co-pays are really bad.  I used to work in the medical field, so I can say that paying cash (that means you pay all at once, no payment plan with the facility) will get you a discount.  Doing pay-as-you-go is fine when you are young and healthy, but risks go up a lot with age.  The problem comes from the unexpected.  Just like car insurance, you only need it when you need it, but you are screwed if you don't have it when you need it.  Medical insurance isn't to make medical costs cheap for regular visits, it's to protect you when life throws a "car accident" at you!  Risks go up if you live alone and don't have a friend to drive you to the hospital if something bad happens suddenly.  

Obviously insurance plans will vary on what coverage you get, but for example, a call to 911 for an ambulance ride will cost you...say $800 without insurance.  Once you get to the hospital, ER Dr.'s charge seperately from the hospital, so you will be getting two bills.  One bill is for the Dr.'s time plus any surgical stuff (like stitches) that they do, the other is all the basic hospital fees that include things like nurses + testing + meds + room + etc.  If you have to stay overnight for any serious accident or illness, that's when things start to get really expensive because people don't ususally stay a single night if they are forced to stay.  Every day is Dr. + hospital room + 24/7 nursecare + testing + meds + meals + etc.  You can't bring in any medication you already own and you are charged for meals whether you eat the hospital food or not.  This continues forever many days until the Dr. clears you to leave.  

One final bit I'll remind everyone.  Hospitals aren't allowed to turn away patients.  Anyone that comes in will get seen.  That's a nice benefit of being in America.  The bad part is that hospitals don't usually get paid when homeless or non-English speaking people don't have insurance and often have to take it as a loss.  Hospitals aren't charity, so that makes the costs for hospitals go up and everyone else ends up taking on a piece of that bill.  Go if you have to, but otherwise stay away from hospitals if you don't have insurance or the bills might be what kills you in the end.
